ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: An object starts from rest and moves along a straight line; the law by which its acceleration changes with time is shown in the figure. Taking the direction in which the object starts moving as the positive direction, which of the following descriptions about the object's motion is correct?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text: At t=2 s, the object's velocity is maximum, equal to 3 m/s.

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: An object starts from rest and moves along a straight line; the law by which its acceleration changes with time is shown in the figure. Taking the direction in which the object starts moving as the positive direction, when does the object's velocity reach its maximum?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure is a graph of acceleration a varying with time t. From 0 to 1 s, the acceleration remains at +2 m/s²; from 1 to 3 s, the acceleration decreases along a straight line, intersecting the time axis at t=2 s, that is, a=0; after 2 s the acceleration is negative, and from 3 to 4 s it remains at -2 m/s². Reasoning: The object starts from rest and moves, and the rate of change of velocity is the acceleration. When the acceleration is positive, the velocity increases; when the acceleration is negative, the velocity decreases. Therefore, the velocity reaches its maximum at the moment when the acceleration changes from positive to negative. It can be seen from the figure that this moment is t=2 s.
